entry.title: A domain controller, a SonicWall, and no malware at all
entry.summary: Two days of hands-on-keyboard on a law firm's domain controller, carried out with two stolen passwords and nothing but built-in Windows tooling. WinRM-driven reconfiguration from a copy-pasted playbook with a typo in it, Kerberoasting the built-in Administrator, a DPAPI domain backup key read off the box, and persistence built entirely out of the firm's own SonicWall SSL-VPN config. Plus the six-group Domain Admins elevation that looked like total compromise and turned out to be the environment's own just-in-time tooling.

entry.title: Fake Claude Install Guide Leads to MacSync Stealer and RAT: What We Pulled From the Attacker's Servers
entry.summary: Reverse engineering MacSync, a six-stage macOS kill chain delivered through malvertised fake Claude installation guides: a Base64 zsh loader, a background daemon function, a 46KB AppleScript stealer, a universal Mach-O RAT beaconing over WebSocket TLS, a signed screen-capture helper, and trojanised Ledger and Trezor wallet apps that phish recovery phrases. Pulled from the attacker's own servers, along with the delivery tier, operator panel, and seed-phrase drop domains.

entry.title: The Devil, Eight Million Emails, and a Whole Lot of Milk
entry.summary: A partner onboarded to Huntress mid-compromise. Within hours we caught an external actor on an internet-facing terminal server running Gammadyne Mailer, broadcasting a Boots UK phishing campaign from 8.9 million addresses to a payload hosted on a compromised Bolivian government website.

entry.title: Let's ClickFix some errors
entry.summary: Walking a Donut + ChromeElevator infostealer chain that started with a single Run-dialog paste. RunMRU, svchost injection, an open payload directory, and a recompiled @xaitax PoC.

entry.title: Komari Red: The Monitoring Tool with a Built-in Reverse Shell
entry.summary: An RMM-disguised attack with a SYSTEM-level reverse shell built into the default install.

entry.title: Threat Advisory: Uptick in Bomgar RMM Exploitation
entry.summary: Threat advisory on attackers exploiting CVE-2026-1731 in Bomgar RMM to deploy LockBit ransomware, create rogue admin accounts, and pivot into MSP customer environments.

entry.title: Supply Chain Compromise of axios npm Package
entry.summary: A compromised maintainer account published backdoored axios versions 1.14.1 and 0.30.4, delivering cross-platform RATs to at least 135 endpoints in the three hours before npm pulled the packages.
